summary: Markets are navigating twin shocks today as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after 33 years, sending the AI chipmaker down 10% premarket and rattling tech stocks, while hawkish Fed commentary following Tuesday's hot CPI print keeps rate-hike expectations elevated. The October CPI rose 0.3% month-over-month for the third consecutive month, above the 0.2% forecast, prompting Fed officials including Waller and Daly to signal openness to a 50-basis-point hike in December. Bitcoin fell below $72,000 as spot ETFs recorded a fifth straight day of outflows totaling $1.44 billion since November 5, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for the bulk of withdrawals. Despite the Nvidia chaos, broader markets held firm Wednesday with the S&P 500 gaining 1.3% and Apple hitting a fresh record at $355.63, though Thursday's premarket showed caution with SPY futures down modestly. Cisco and Applied Materials report earnings after the close, with AI infrastructure demand in focus.

signals.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid China chip scandal, stock plunges 10%
signals.desc: Jensen Huang's abrupt exit after 33 years has rattled AI infrastructure stocks, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and DOJ launching antitrust probe into Nvidia, Megaspeed, and Supermicro.

signals.title: Hot October CPI fuels 50-bp December hike speculation
signals.desc: Core CPI rose 0.3% for the third straight month, topping forecasts, while Fed's Waller and Logan opened the door to faster tightening and markets now price nearly 60 basis points of hikes through March 2027.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs bleed $1.44B in five-day outflow streak
signals.desc: Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded fifth consecutive day of withdrawals on November 11, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $269.73 million as BTC fell below $72,000 and year-to-date flows turned negative at -$1.42 billion.

signals.title: AMD surges 6% on analyst upgrade amid Nvidia turmoil
signals.desc: Advanced Micro Devices rallied as investors bet on competitive advantages from Nvidia's leadership crisis, with Broadcom also gaining on expectations of AI chip market share shifts.

signals.title: Apple hits record high as mega-cap tech diverges
signals.desc: AAPL closed at all-time high of $355.63 Wednesday, up 2%, showing resilience in tech even as Nvidia drama and rising rates pressure growth stocks, with S&P 500 up 1.3%.

verdict: Leadership vacuum at Nvidia and hawkish Fed pivot create near-term volatility, but resilient mega-cap earnings and selective sector rotation suggest markets will digest shocks rather than crater.
